To the best of our knowledge, this is the first method to discover an update rule for an agent in general-sum games. DUOS meta-trains the rule to maximise the agent's expected return over its lifetime, and updates an inner network using the agent's own experience. We show that our discovered rule exhibits behaviour consistent with opponent shaping without reading opponent policies or parameters, and ranks 1st in normalised mean score and 1st in self-play among tournament entrants.

papers.title: Cultural Adaptation within Repeated Social Interactions
papers.abstract: Much of human culture is tacit and is typically learned through situated social interaction. As LLMs are deployed as interactive agents across diverse communities, assessing their cultural competence demands moving beyond existing question-answering approaches, shifting from what they know to how they adapt. In this work, we broaden the scope of cultural adaptation in NLP by investigating whether LLMs can adapt through repeated interactions via a sandbox environment. By reframing cultural adaptation as a continuous process of norm assimilation through social interaction, our work demonstrates that memory mechanisms foster longitudinal learning across repeated interactions, facilitate transfer to different social settings, and enable multilingual norm assimilation across five languages. Together, our findings lay the groundwork for continuous, interaction-driven cultural adaptation in LLMs.

papers.title: Butler's conjecture for K3 curves
papers.abstract: Butler's conjectures predict that, on a general smooth curve $C$ of genus $g\ge3$, a general coherent system $[\mathcal{O}_C\otimes V\xrightarrowφE]$ with semistable underlying bundle $E$ and $\dim V>\operatorname{rk}(E)$ has surjective evaluation map $φ$ and stable kernel. In this paper, we prove Butler's conjectures for $g\ge8$ in the two cases in which the Brill-Noether geometry of a general curve is known, namely rank one and the range $μ(E)>2g-2$. By deformation and openness, it suffices to establish the result on a single Brill-Noether-Petri general curve. We do so for curves on K3 surfaces of Picard rank one, using the wall-crossing theory of coherent systems developed by the first two authors.

papers.title: The complex periodic variability of PKS 0301-243: hints of a supermassive black hole binary candidate
papers.abstract: In hierarchical galaxy formation, supermassive black hole binaries are a ubiquitous consequence of frequent galaxy mergers, yet subparsec binaries remain difficult to be confirmed. Periodic flux modulations may arise from the orbital motion of black holes in close binaries, while relativistic jet precession can provide an additional source of periodic variability. Such periodic signatures therefore motivate us to identify close binary candidates. Here, we report an optical periodicity of $269^{+13}_{-14}$ days in both Zwicky Transient Facility g and r bands of the blazar PKS 0301-243, with corrected global significances of $2.75σ$ and $2.18σ$, respectively. This signal persists over 7 cycles across a baseline of ~2000 days. We interpret this period as a possible modulation associated with the orbital motion of a supermassive black hole binary. A longer optical periodicity of $889^{+47}_{-46}$ days is identified in Katzman Automatic Imaging Telescope, with corrected global significance of $1.97σ$. The longer periodicity spans approximately 5 cycles over a baseline of ~4500 days, potentially associated with jet precession. Both periodicities are independently identified using multiple methods. A supermassive black hole binary incorporating a relativistic jet and a circumbinary disc could reproduce the observed light curve ensemble. For a total mass of $10^{8.95} M_\odot$ and a mass ratio q = 0.1, the derived milli-parsec separation and a short gravitational wave driven coalescence time, $t_c = 1122^{+144}_{-144}$ years, imply that PKS 0301-243 may be a rare source of nano-hertz gravitational waves and a potential multimessenger laboratory for the terminal stages of supermassive black hole coalescence.

papers.title: Electromagnetically Consistent Monostatic ISAC Beamforming: Mutual Coupling, Active Mismatch and Tx-Rx Leakage in Compact Dipole Arrays
papers.abstract: Beamforming for integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) is usually designed on ideal array manifolds with a norm constraint on the transmit signal. In a compact monostatic transceiver this hides three antenna effects: distorted embedded patterns, beam-dependent active mismatch at the power amplifiers, and transmit-to-receive leakage that raises the radar noise floor. We build a multiport scattering model of a shared-aperture dipole array directly from method-of-moments simulations and use it to formulate a Cramer-Rao bound minimizing ISAC beamformer with multiuser SINR constraints, per-port active reflection constraints and a leakage budget, solved as a semidefinite program with a one-dimensional budget search. Full-wave evaluation shows that coupling-unaware designs miss their SINR targets by up to 6.2 dB and drive amplifiers to an equivalent VSWR above 3.3 at small spacings. For spacings from 0.3 to 0.5 wavelengths, the proposed design meets all targets with an equivalent VSWR below 2 and lowers the root Cramer-Rao bound by 32 to 53 percent for 80 dB of self-interference cancellation and by a factor of 3.4 to 5.6 for 70 dB. An independent finite-difference time-domain model of the final layout in openEMS confirms that the leakage null and the ranking of the designs are preserved.

papers.title: InstantHand: Feed-Forward 3D Gaussian Splatting for Animatable Hand Avatar Reconstruction from a Single Image
papers.abstract: Hand avatar reconstruction typically relies on multi-view capture or per-subject optimization, limiting its scalability. We introduce InstantHand, a feed-forward framework that constructs an animatable 3D Gaussian hand avatar from a single image using off-the-shelf MANO, camera, and mask estimates, without test-time optimization. Image-averaged losses provide insufficient supervision for alpha leakage, which thickens thin finger contours. To address this issue, we propose a Soft Alpha Band regularizer that concentrates supervision on silhouette boundaries. Furthermore, colors regressed from image features can drift toward a learned prior even in observed regions. Our Reliability-gated Appearance Transfer preserves observed appearance by transferring source colors according to each Gaussian's rendering contribution, while completing unobserved regions using the learned prior conditioned on global source identity. InstantHand constructs an avatar in 2.84 seconds and renders at 161 FPS, matching per-subject-optimized baselines on InterHand2.6M and remaining competitive in zero-shot evaluation on HanCo.

papers.title: GNS-like representations of a quasi *-algebra in Krein spaces
papers.abstract: In this paper unbounded representations of quasi *-algebras on an indefinite inner product space are introduced and studied. After introducing the partial *-algebra of unbounded closable operators sharing a common dense domain in a Krein space, the appropriate notion of *-representation in this setting is developed, and a GNS-type construction for quasi *-algebras based on $α$-positive sesquilinear forms is established. Furthermore, the notion of abstract conditional expectation is generalized to quasi *-algebras and how \emph{admissible} abstract conditional expectations $P$ give rise to representable $P$-forms is shown. The relation between $α$-positive forms and $P$-forms is also clarified. Several examples are provided.

papers.title: Reprogrammable polaritonic skyrmion and meron lattices based on the phase-change material In$_3$SbTe$_2$
papers.abstract: Optical topological quasiparticles such as skyrmions and merons consist of engineered electromagnetic fields which can be realized via the controlled interference of polaritons. The resulting polaritonic topological lattices offer a promising platform for on-chip information encoding and nanoscale light-matter interaction. However, realizing these functionalities requires active tailoring of the polaritonic topological lattice. Although previous works have achieved tuning of the size of the polaritonic lattice sites, these methods relied on cumbersome and time-consuming fabrication processes and do not allow reconfiguration of the topological invariant. Here, we demonstrate fast optical prototyping of reconfigurable hexagonal and square coupling structures for the generation of polaritonic topological lattices with hyperbolic phonon polaritons in hBN using the phase-change material In$_3$SbTe$_2$. As In$_3$SbTe$_2$ can be switched reversibly between its dielectric ($\varepsilon$>0) amorphous and metallic ($\varepsilon$<0) crystalline phase by laser pulses, metallic In$_3$SbTe$_2$ coupling structures can be optically programmed and reconfigured. Our approach enables tailoring the size of the topological lattice sites by tuning the incident frequency. Moreover, In$_3$SbTe$_2$ allows for tailoring the topological invariant by reprogramming the coupling structure. Our platform enables reprogramming of robust optical topologies within minutes, opening a route toward rewritable on-chip photonic computing based on robust and on demand reconfigurable topological states.

papers.title: Exploring the limit of partonic collectivity in small collision systems at the LHC
papers.abstract: The existence of a partonic phase in small collision systems has been investigated previously through measurements of the elliptic flow ($v_{2}$) of mesons ($π^{\pm}$, K$^{\pm}$, and K$_{S}^{0}$) and baryons ($\rm{p}(\overline{\rm{p}})$, $Λ(\overlineΛ)$) in high-multiplicity p-Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}} = 5.02$ TeV and pp collisions at $\sqrt{s} = 13$ TeV recorded by ALICE. The results have revealed a grouping and splitting behavior of $v_{2}$ for baryons and mesons at intermediate transverse momentum ($p_{\rm{T}}$), establishing that partonic collectivity, as observed in heavy-ion collisions, is also present in these systems. In this Letter, the $p_{\rm{T}}$-differential $v_{2}$ of various hadronic species is investigated in p-Pb collisions for the multiplicity intervals $N_{\rm ch} \geq 50$, $25 \leq N_{\rm ch} < 50$, and $15 \leq N_{\rm ch} < 25$, as well as in pp collisions for $25 \leq N_{\rm ch} < 50$ and $15 \leq N_{\rm ch} < 25$. Here, $N_{\rm ch}$ is the efficiency-corrected number of charged particles produced in the kinematic region of $|η|< 0.8$ and $0.2 < p_{\rm T} < 3.0$ GeV/$c$. The characteristic mass dependence of $v_{2}$, as well as the grouping and splitting patterns among identified particles, are examined. The results in both p-Pb and pp collisions with $N_{\rm ch} \geq 25$ are consistent with the development of partonic collectivity. In the low-multiplicity region, $15 \leq N_{\rm ch} < 25$, the baryon-to-meson $v_{2}$ splitting, as quantified by the baryon-to-meson $v_2$ ratios, remains broadly consistent with that at higher multiplicities. However, its significance decreases to $\sim2σ$ in p-Pb collisions and to less than $1σ$ in pp collisions owing to the sizable experimental uncertainties. These measurements constitute the first steps towards identifying the limits of partonic flow in small collision systems at the LHC.

papers.title: Oriented V-systems
papers.abstract: We introduce the notion of an oriented $\vee$-system which gives a class of solutions of the oriented associativity equations generalising Veselov's $\vee$-system solutions of WDVV equations. An oriented $\vee$-system is a special configuration of pairs of a vector and a covector in a linear space. We show that the class of oriented $\vee$-systems is closed under taking subsystems and restrictions. We provide examples which include a multiparameter family related to imprimitive complex reflection groups.

papers.title: Decision Models as Retrieval Gates Against Injection and Pollution
papers.abstract: Retrieved web text can carry instructions aimed at the language model, or synthetic pages written to mislead. We test whether released open-weight decision models, which answer typed questions about a text without generating tokens, can screen retrieved passages against both threats. On a benchmark of 1,000 questions over forum-style web pages with hidden injected instructions, a Kev-4B gate reads each passage's HTML. Attack success, measured automatically, falls from 27.9% with no defence to 13.6% with the published mitigations (sanitisation, normalisation and citation prompting) and to 5.7% with the gate added. The gate takes 76 ms per passage and wrongly flags 4 of 186 benign pages with instructions for human readers. Responsiveness on clean queries stays within a point (85.6% to 86.2%). On a 200-query pollution testbed where two thirds of the candidate pages are fake, filtering the pool before the top ten are chosen keeps fake pages out of the answer (0.5% exposure) and holds accuracy at 83%, against 28% with no filter. Filtering only the top ten leaves the generator too few pages to answer. Large LLMs used as judges rank attacks better (AUROC 0.99 against 0.94) but cost ten times more. Gates catch more attacks when they read the page's HTML than when they read its plain text. Every model is open-weight.

papers.title: Typical number and stability of equilibria in large non-reciprocal complex systems
papers.abstract: We consider a prototypical class of dynamics of $N\gg 1$ degrees of freedom subject to two competing terms, one favoring relaxation to a trivial equilibrium and one taking the form of a Gaussian force field promoting the emergence of many local equilibria. The latter is a non-gradient field, i.e. it includes a non-reciprocal component with a tunable strength. For this model, we compute the quenched complexity, i.e. the exponential growth rate of the typical number of equilibria, resolved by stability index. We compare it with the annealed complexity, i.e. the exponential growth rate of the average number of equilibria. We show that the two coincide only in the fully non-reciprocal limit: for any finite degree of reciprocity, typical realizations contain exponentially fewer equilibria than predicted by the average count. Increasing reciprocity enhances the discrepancy between the two. The quenched complexity depends explicitly on the covariance of the random force field and on the degree of non-reciprocity: the universality observed at the annealed level breaks down. The average counting of equilibria correctly identifies the location of the topology trivialization transition, but it does not capture the typical organization of equilibria near this transition, nor the stability index of the dominant equilibria.

papers.title: Polarity Classification with Multitask Learning Syntax Augmentation
papers.abstract: Sentiment Analysis (SA) is a fundamental NLP task concerned with the identification and categorization of subjective information in text. While lexicon-based methods offer transparency, they often struggle with linguistic phenomena such as negation and intensification. Syntactic parsing has been integrated into SA pipelines to address this, but conventional parsers introduce significant computational overhead. Recent work shows that reformulating dependency parsing as a Sequence Labeling (SEL) task can improve efficiency. We propose and compare two strategies for integrating syntactic knowledge into a neural sentiment analysis model under unified Multi-Task Learning (MTL). The first, Standard-MTL, jointly learns dependency parsing (via sequence labeling) and sentiment polarity classification using a shared encoder with two task-specific heads. The second, Contrastive-MTL, provides implicit syntactic guidance through a contrastive auxiliary objective and a syntax-biased attention pooling mechanism, without requiring explicit label prediction. Both rely on syntactic annotations during training and eliminate need for hand-crafted compositional rules or external parsing at inference. We evaluate eleven datasets spanning seven languages---the MARC corpus (English, Spanish, French, German) and seven datasets from SemEval-2022 Task 10 (English, Spanish, Norwegian, Basque, Catalan)---using four established SEL encodings. With the relative encoding, Contrastive-MTL outperforms a syntax-naive baseline on 10 of 11 datasets and surpasses the external rule-based pipeline (SELSP) that parses at inference on all six datasets where the latter applies, while being 1.5--9$\times$ faster at evaluation. Standard-MTL is more dataset- and encoding-dependent. These results show implicit syntactic supervision during training can match or exceed explicit parsing at inference without computational overhead.

papers.title: Instabilities of Simpson-Visser black bounces sourced by a phantom scalar and nonlinear electrodynamics
papers.abstract: We study the linear stability of Simpson-Visser ``black-bounce'' space-times (regular black holes and wormholes) under spherically symmetric (monopole) perturbations, taking as a source a phantom scalar field with a self-interaction potential and a magnetic field within nonlinear electrodynamics (NED). The metric contains two parameters: the mass $M$ and the bounce parameter $a >0$, such that $a \leq 2M$ corresponds to black holes and $a > 2M$ to wormholes. The stability problem reduces to a boundary-value problem for a Schrödinger-like equation with a certain effective potential. All space-times under study are found to be unstable, and the corresponding exponential growth rates are calculated. For black holes the results are obtained without complications, while the wormhole stability problem faces difficulties that seem to be previously unnoticed. Thus, the Darboux transformation, used to remove the wall shaped $\approx 2/z^2$ in the effective potentials at wormhole throats ($z$ is the tortoise coordinate), creates nonphysical poles outside the throat for $a/(2M) \lesssim 4.98$. We circumvent this difficulty by using a gauge-invariant approach in the spirit of Cremona, Pizzocchero and Sarbach, leading to a master equation with a simple and regular potential. Its further analysis reveals unstable modes: the mode with a variable throat radius is always present; for $a/(2M) \gtrsim 4.98$ there are two real growing throat modes, which merge into a complex-conjugate pair (oscillatory instability) for smaller $a$. A further analysis reveals three exceptional points that separate ranges of $a/(2M)$ with different perturbation regimes. Furthermore, the leading unstable black-hole and wormhole modes approach the same limiting growth rate $Mκ\simeq 0.10121$ as $a/(2M)$ approaches unity from either side.

papers.title: ControlAnything: Generative UI and On-Demand Device Integration for Mixed-Reality Hand Interaction by a Coding Agent
papers.abstract: Connecting hand input in mixed reality (MR) to a nearby physical device typically requires an integration written in advance for that device, its transport and the mapping. ControlAnything defers this integration to the moment of use and assigns it to a coding agent. On a Meta Quest 3, the wearer selects an object outlined by SAM 3.1 and states what their hands should control. An agent built on Meta's Muse Spark model then writes a connector program on the wearer's laptop, tests it against the live device through hand-written MIDI, Bluetooth and key-press transports, and returns augmented-reality (AR) controls, a per-frame hand program, or both. These outputs are a form of generative UI, interfaces created by an AI model; here, the agent also generates and tests the code that binds the interface to a physical device. In a single-session technical evaluation with the author as the only wearer, nine of ten requests addressing five targets reached a ready state, and the wearer stopped one. The median time to ready was 32.5 s (range 24.9-57.8 s, excluding speech transcription); sequential model calls accounted for a median of 89.9% of this time, and 91.7% of input tokens came from the prompt cache. The system's evidence of success extends to transport acknowledgements but not to physical effects. These findings point to connector reuse and the observation of effects through the headset's own sensors as next steps for on-demand device integration in MR. A user study with first-time wearers is planned.

papers.title: Hypercyclic and topologically transitive semigroups of composition operators (revised and extended version)
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a separable locally compact metric space, let $E\neq\{0\}$ be a normed space, and let $G$ be a semigroup of continuous self-maps of $X$. Every $φ\in G$ induces the composition operator $C_φf=f\circφ$ on the space $C(X,E)$ of continuous functions endowed with the compact-open topology. We characterize the topological transitivity of the semigroup $\widehat{G}=\{C_φ:φ\in G\}$ by a condition that combines the run-away property of $G$ with an approximate form of injectivity, and we show that, when $E$ is separable, $\widehat{G}$ is topologically transitive if and only if it is hypercyclic. In particular, if every element of $G$ is one-to-one and $G$ is run-away, then $\widehat{G}$ is topologically transitive, and hypercyclic when $E$ is separable. For a single map $φ$ we obtain: $C_φ$ is hypercyclic $\iff$ $C_φ$ is topologically transitive $\iff$ $φ$ is one-to-one and run-away, and $C_φ$ is mixing $\iff$ $φ$ is one-to-one and strongly run-away. If, moreover, $φ$ is an open map (which is automatic on manifolds by invariance of domain), then $C_φ$ is Devaney chaotic. On an open interval all of these properties are equivalent to $φ$ being one-to-one without fixed points.

papers.title: An order-reversing embedding of Turing degrees into Arthur-Nimue-Merlin degrees (short version)
papers.abstract: The Arthur-Nimue-Merlin degrees are a generalization of the Turing degrees introduced by Kihara as a tangible description of the partially ordered set of Lawvere-Tierney topologies on the effective topos (equivalently, subtoposes of the effective topos). They are defined in terms of a three-player game that introduces both angelic and demonic non-determinism into oracle queries. We construct an order embedding of the Turing degrees with their order reversed into the Arthur-Nimue-Merlin degrees, whose image we call the "co-Turing degrees"; we then study the order relationship of these co-Turing degrees with the (naturally embedded) Turing degrees within the Arthur-Nimue-Merlin degrees. This is a short version of arXiv:2603.19946, focused on the main results.

papers.title: Learning the Task or Learning the Verifier? Rethinking Criteria Exposure in Embodied Self-Improvement
papers.abstract: Self-improving embodied agents are increasingly being developed and compared on robot simulation benchmarks. Several recent works expose the benchmark's success criteria to the learning agent, a practice we call Criteria Exposure (CE). These criteria, originally written to verify policies trained by imitation learning, often demand more than the corresponding language instructions, so a score from such a verifier may not faithfully reflect whether the instructed task was completed, especially for robot-control programs written by an agent. As embodied coding agents report ever higher benchmark scores, a natural question arises: when a coding agent is exposed to the benchmark's criteria, does it generate code that better performs the instructed task, or code that simply overfits to the verification criteria? We conduct controlled experiments with a self-improving agent with and without CE, and find that with CE the agent quickly produces code with a higher success rate under the given criteria, but this advantage disappears when the criteria are changed slightly without departing from the original instructions. More importantly, the skills the agent develops under CE transfer poorly across tasks. We further propose instruction-faithful criteria and show that they better reflect the performance of agent-generated programs.

papers.title: Random Fibonacci Tilings
papers.abstract: The Fibonacci spiral is formed by a square-joining rule: begin with a unit square and attach squares whose side lengths follow the Fibonacci sequence; in the standard construction, choices of direction produce a spiral and a tiling of the plane. We study a randomization of this construction, in which the attachment axis alternates deterministically, while fair coin flips determine direction. For a lattice point we ask when the growing rectangle first covers that point and how the expected covering time depends on its location. Tracking the rectangle's boundary reduces this question to random subset sums of even- and odd-indexed Fibonacci numbers. We extend the construction to d dimensions, where coordinate subsequences are super-increasing, allowing us to derive exact covering probabilities and formulas for the expectation and variance. For $d\geq2$, the expected covering time grows logarithmically with distance from the initial block, while the variance remains uniformly bounded. We obtain exponential tail bounds for the delay beyond the earliest feasible covering stage. Finally, we extend the Fibonacci spiral to the randomized tiling through a square-by-square construction using circular arcs and quintic connectors. This construction uses one-step lookahead, admits a continuously differentiable parameterization, and recovers the Fibonacci spiral for the standard tiling.

papers.title: $p$-parity conjecture for Panchishkin Galois representations
papers.abstract: Let $p$ be an odd prime, and let $V_1$ and $V_2$ be symplectic self-dual $p$-adic de Rham representations of $G_{\mathbb{Q}}$ that are pure (of weight $-1$) and satisfy the Panchishkin condition at $p$. Suppose that $V_1$ and $V_2$ are residually isomorphic, compatibly with their Panchishkin filtrations. We prove the relative $p$-parity conjecture relating the ratio of the global root numbers of $V_1$ and $V_2$ to the difference of their Bloch-Kato Selmer dimensions. We have no restriction on the dimension of the Galois representation, the Hodge-Tate weights or the monodromy operator at $p$, and the residual isomorphism need not be symplectic. The proof expresses ratios of local root numbers in terms of local invariants over the cyclotomic $\mathbb{Z}_p$-extension: a new invariant introduced at $p$, and local Iwasawa $λ$-invariants at $\ell\neq p$. Both are compatible with the arithmetic local constants of Mazur-Rubin and Nekovář. A key input, proved using Sen theory, is that the Bloch-Kato and strict local conditions at $p$ coincide over the cyclotomic $\mathbb{Z}_p$-extension, generalising results of Coates-Greenberg and Nekovář. As applications, we obtain new cases of the $p$-parity conjecture, including cases of rank greater than two: Artin twists of CM Hida families, orthogonal Artin twists of ordinary modular forms, symmetric cubes along Hida families, and families of abelian surfaces, together with unconditional numerical examples.

papers.title: Benchmarking Large Language Models on Heterogeneous Cognitive and Biomedical Knowledge Graphs: The Role of Graph Grounding in Multi-Hop Reasoning and Hallucination Mitigation
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used in biomedical and cognitive neuroscience, but their ability to reason reliably over heterogeneous knowledge graphs (KGs) remains unclear. We benchmark five LLMs (GPT-5.1, Gemini 2.0 Pro, Llama 3, Qwen, and BioGPT) across five KGs: DrugBank, NeuroSynth, Cognitive Atlas, Brain Map, and GDPKG. We introduce a multitier query dataset to evaluate reasoning depth and factual accuracy under KG-aware (graph-grounded) and KG-agnostic conditions. Inter-annotator agreement was substantial, with Cohen's kappa of 0.781 (range: 0.753-0.807) and Fleiss' kappa of 0.77. Results show that general-purpose models, particularly GPT-5.1 and Gemini 2.0 Pro, generally outperform domain-specific models on multi-hop and high-level reasoning tasks, although performance declines as query complexity increases. KG grounding reduces hallucination rates across all evaluated models. Contrary to our initial hypothesis, domain-specific models do not consistently outperform general-purpose models on specialized tasks without graph grounding. These findings highlight the value of combining broad language-model capabilities with structured domain knowledge. We provide practical guidance for selecting LLM-KG integration strategies based on task complexity and computational constraints, and discuss hybrid neurosymbolic architectures for personalized medicine, cognitive disorder diagnosis, and explainable AI.

papers.title: Interpretable many-body interaction laws for collective motion from few trajectories
papers.abstract: Models of collective motion usually reduce social interactions to pairwise forces, despite empirical evidence for many-body effects. We introduce the directional atomic cluster expansion (dACE), which adapts the atomic cluster expansion (ACE) of interatomic potentials to self-propelled agents. dACE provides a systematically improvable, exactly equivariant expansion of an agent's acceleration that splits uniquely into 1-, 2-, 3-body and higher contributions, along with a self term for the agent's own past motion that is fitted so that it does not absorb the interactions. On simulated collectives in two and three dimensions with known rules, dACE recovers the interaction law body order by body order from little data, while the neural model SocialNet, the current closest competitor, needs more data, has much larger errors on many-body or chiral rules and is restricted to 2D. On real data sets of tracked zebrafish and golden shiners, the laws learned by dACE agree better between disjoint halves of the data than SocialNet's. The learned laws are interpretable, and in the shiners the 3-body term opposes the pairwise response as neighbourhoods get dense. Finally, we show that next-step prediction accuracy mostly measures self-propulsion and noise rather than the interactions, and suggest more robust combinations of error measures for interaction learning.

papers.title: Testing Gravitationally-Induced-Entanglement with Massive Particles and Quantum Clocks
papers.abstract: We present an experimental proposal to test whether gravity can entangle a levitated particle with an array of quantum clocks. By harnessing the collective interaction between a micrometer-scale particle and an array of ultra-precise nuclear clocks, our scheme offers a conceivable path to observing gravitationally mediated entanglement with quantum clocks in the laboratory. Crucially, this setup will probe a genuinely relativistic effect one that requires the contribution of internal clock energy to active gravitational mass and cannot arise from the Newtonian interaction between fixed masses. Therefore, observing this entanglement would provide evidence for the quantised nature of active gravitational mass -- which has not been tested in any prior experiment -- rather than for spatial coherence of fixed masses,which is routinely tested in matterwave interferometers

papers.title: Trilemma: How Agents choose between Honesty, Confidentiality, and Task Completion
papers.abstract: Personal AI agents often act on underspecified instructions and draw on context such as their user's messages and calendar to decide how to proceed. This context can contain private preferences that interfere with the task, with other people's interests, or with confidentiality norms. Prior work has studied deception under goal conflicts and the leakage of private information, but largely as separate problems. We study both problems together in a simulated company Slack workspace in which four employees delegate sprint staffing to personal agents. Two agents learn from private messages that their employee avoids working with a particular colleague. Because the other agents request justifications for task preferences and the only true justification is confidential, the agents cannot simultaneously remain honest, preserve confidentiality, and complete the staffing. We evaluate seven open-weight models and Claude and GPT models. Of the 135/140 open-weight agents that pursue the avoidance preference, 107 either make false claims about task fit or logistics or cite a true consideration as if it were their actual reason. In a three-model comparison, confidentiality instructions reduce disclosure of the preference from 83% (none) to 31% (medium) to 2% (strong). However, the task is often not completed anyway; in the main experiment (medium confidentiality instructions), only 16 of 70 runs end with a valid staffing. In their reasoning traces, agents frequently acknowledge evidence against their claims and still conclude that the claims are not false; they engage in motivated reasoning. Our results indicate that agents can strategically make false or misleading claims in a day-to-day task without being instructed to; the environment provides a controlled testbed for studying how agents resolve such conflicts and for developing deception monitors.

papers.title: LLM-Assisted Label Noise Correction for EEG-Based Sleep Stage Classification
papers.abstract: Automatic sleep stage classification from electroencephalography (EEG) signals is a critical task in clinical sleep medicine. While deep learning models have shown promising results in this domain, their performance is fundamentally constrained by the quality of training labels, which human experts manually annotate and that are subject to inter-rater disagreement and systematic labeling errors. In this paper, we propose a novel LLM-assisted label-noise filtering pipeline that operates exclusively during training to identify and remove unreliable sleep-stage annotations before retraining the classifier. Specifically, TinySleepNet is first trained on the original dataset to extract per-epoch SoftMax confidence scores, then low-confidence epochs are submitted to LLaMA 3.1 along with their EEG spectral features and surrounding sequence context. The LLM evaluates each epoch against AASM sleep-scoring guidelines and assigns a verdict of RELIABLE or SUSPICIOUS. Suspicious epochs are removed from the training set, and TinySleepNet is retrained on the cleaned data. Evaluated on the Sleep-EDF Expanded dataset using 20-fold cross-validation, our method improves overall accuracy from 81.8% to 84.6% and Macro F1-score from 75.6% to 77.4%, with particularly notable gains in REM detection. Crucially, because the LLM operates only during training, the lightweight TinySleepNet architecture (1.3M parameters) is preserved at inference, making the proposed pipeline suitable for real-time, wearable sleep monitoring applications.

papers.title: Recovery gates as a resource in repetition-code process tomography: exhaustive gate-optimal designs for three, five and seven qubits
papers.abstract: Process tomography built on stabilizer codes compares the logical channel of a repetition code with a reference channel, and the decoder that produces that channel is almost always fixed to the standard minimum-weight one. We ask how many physical single-qubit Pauli gates the decoder actually needs when the measurement basis is fixed---the constraint under which the count is a resource rather than a bookkeeping artefact. Exhaustive enumeration of every recovery design for $n=3$, $5$ and $7$ qubits, with rank decided by exact modular arithmetic at two primes, gives minimal counts of $0$, $1$ and $5$ gates, against $6$, $10$ and $14$ for first-order decoding and $6$, $50$ and $308$ for full minimum-weight decoding. The count depends only on how many sites are corrected and never on which, so the two halves of the design problem separate. Correcting more sites is not monotonically better: at $n=7$ full decoding loses three dimensions of rank, and under a calibration-residual floor the precision curve at $n=3$ is U-shaped. The three-gate design is $9.5$ times more precise than the standard six-gate decoder at the median of $40$ sampled working points, and more precise at every one of them ($1.8$ to $88$ times); the size of that factor belongs to the working point, the ordering does not. Reaching a $10$\,mrad rms error then costs $1.2\times10^{7}$ shots in $65$\,s on a current superconducting device at a well-conditioned point, while $n\ge5$ stays out of reach for conditioning reasons rather than gate-count reasons. Finally, the optimal designs are not covariant under chain reversal: they separate the mirror pair of arXiv:2610.19779 by $1.3\times10^{-3}$ while leaving the Jacobian at full rank.

papers.title: The isoperimetric problem in the Riemannian Heisenberg $3$-space
papers.abstract: We prove that every closed weakly stable constant mean curvature surface immersed in the Riemannian Heisenberg space ${\rm Nil}_3$ is an embedded rotational sphere. As a consequence, we solve the isoperimetric problem in ${\rm Nil}_3$: the isoperimetric domains of ${\rm Nil}_3$ are exactly the regions enclosed by rotational constant mean curvature spheres, and for each prescribed volume there is a unique such domain, up to ambient isometry. For small volumes, the isoperimetric result was proved by Tomter in 1993.

papers.title: RM-VLM: From Natural-Language Task Descriptions to Vision-Grounded Reward Machines
papers.abstract: Reward machines (RMs) have been proposed as a reward formulation in reinforcement learning (RL) to capture non-Markovian tasks where credit assignment depends on history. By representing reward functions as automata, RMs expose the task's temporal structure and allow such rewards to be handled within a Markovian framework. However, they assume a labelling function, a proposition-grounding oracle for observations, which must be manually engineered for each environment, limiting their wider applicability. In this work, we address this limitation by proposing RM-VLM, a novel approach in which a large language model (LLM) generates an RM from a natural-language task description, and a vision-language model (VLM) acts as the labelling function, grounding the RM's propositions over image-based observations during RM-guided policy learning. A VLM-based value function estimator is used to assess the agent's progress towards each RM transition and derive a dense reward signal. We evaluate RM-VLM on three domains covering non-Markovian grid-world navigation, robotic manipulation, and 3D object collection. Our experimental results show that RM-VLM consistently achieves higher task success rates than existing VLM-based reward methods across all tested domains.

papers.title: Measured Coupling for Parallel Decoding in Diffusion Language Models
papers.abstract: Diffusion language models can write many tokens per step, but must choose which tokens are safe to commit together. Mean-field decoding penalizes pairs of positions whose predictions look alike. We replace this proxy with the coupling itself: how much committing one token changes the model's confidence at another. Cheap probes inside the main forward pass measure it, with no training or extra model, and it plugs into the same mean-field rule. On three models and four benchmarks, our method needs far fewer steps than mean-field decoding and is faster in most settings, also with a key-value cache, at an average accuracy cost of 1.1 points. Shuffling the couplings or replacing them with a uniform bonus loses this gain.

papers.title: GINGER: Spicing Up Graph-Based Vector Search
papers.abstract: We present \textsc{Ginger}, a state-of-the-art open-source C++ library for graph-based approximate nearest neighbor search (ANNS). We developed \textsc{Ginger} at Google to push the speed and memory efficiency of graph search on large and high-dimensional embedding datasets. \textsc{Ginger} surpasses existing ANNS libraries with regards to query throughput and indexing time while matching the memory footprint of the most space-efficient competitors. \textsc{Ginger} builds upon recent advances in proximity graph construction (PiPNN) and vector quantization (TurboQuant). We introduce Nested TurboQuant (NTQ), a two-level quantizer which supports low precision graph navigation and high precision reranking in a single code. This representation achieves near floating point precision with $2.6\times$ less memory. We also compress the size of our proximity graphs by up to $2.5\times$ without impacting query throughput. We combine graph reordering with a new lossless compression codec called AdaptiveGap, which builds upon StreamVByte. At $95\%$ recall, \textsc{Ginger} speeds up query throughput by an average of $1.8\times$ over each dataset's fastest competitor and by at least $2.3\times$ over any single library. This lead grows to $2.9\times$ over compact libraries on high-dimensional embeddings.

papers.title: The Proof Analysis Problem for Constant-Depth Frege
papers.abstract: We give a parallel algorithm for the Proof Analysis Problem of Arteche, Atserias, de Rezende, and Khaniki (FOCS 2025). The problem asks, given a CNF formula $φ$ on $n$ variables and a proof $π$ of a size-$s$ Resolution lower bound on $φ$, encoded as $\neg \mathrm{Ref}_s(φ)$, to extract a satisfying assignment for $φ$ when one exists. The original work gave a polynomial-time extraction algorithm for Resolution refutations that enabled a formalization of the Atserias-Müller lower bound (FOCS 2019) in Extended Frege, but it appeared inherently sequential. We devise a new algorithm that performs assignment extraction in low-depth circuit classes. Specifically, we give an assignment extraction algorithm computable by polynomial-size $\mathbf{TC}^0$ circuits and by quasipolynomial-size $\mathbf{AC}^0$ circuits, and we prove the correctness of the latter within quasipolynomial-size $\mathbf{AC}^0$-Frege. This is thanks to a new formalization of the Atserias-Müller lower bound in the relativized theory $\mathsf{T}^4_2(α)$ of bounded arithmetic, which corresponds to depth-$4$ Frege systems. This yields quasipolynomial-size $\mathbf{AC}^0$-Frege proofs for a broad class of Resolution lower bounds, making progress on a question of Pudlák. A key feature of our approach is an improved parameter regime where we get $\mathbf{AC}^0$-Frege formalizations of Resolution lower bounds $\neg \mathrm{Ref}_s(φ)$ for all $s$, including $s = n^{O(1)}$. W also show that the Proof Analysis Problem for $\mathbf{AC}^0$-Frege is $\mathbf{NP}$-hard under quasipolynomial-time reductions, which rules out certain Atserias-Müller-type approaches to the hardness of automating constant-depth Frege. Furthermore, automating $\mathbf{AC}^0$-Frege on Resolution lower bound formulas suffices to automate it on all formulas.

papers.title: Hardness of integer linear feasibility with cyclic support
papers.abstract: We prove that integer linear feasibility is strongly $NP$-complete even when the constraint matrix has exactly two nonzero entries in every row and column, with its support forming a single cycle. This holds already for monotone systems (one positive and one negative coefficient in each inequality) with nonzero coefficients of absolute value $2$ or $3$ and right-hand sides in $\{-1,0,1,2\}$. No variable bounds are supplied separately from the system. For systems in which each inequality involves at most two variables, this strengthens known hardness results by restricting all numerical data to fixed finite sets. For systems in which each variable occurs in at most two inequalities, this establishes, to the best of our knowledge, the first $NP$-hardness result for feasibility. We also give negative answers, unless $P=NP$, to questions on polynomial-time solvability of integer programs with bounded coefficients and bounded totally $Δ$-modular treewidth, and on fixed-parameter tractability of integer bound propagation with respect to coefficient and right-hand-side magnitudes.

papers.title: First-Token Attraction in Mamba Dynamics
papers.abstract: We study token dynamics in deep Mamba models, with a particular focus on the attracting role of the first token. Unlike attention mechanisms, where token interactions are governed by positive scalar coefficients, Mamba dynamics involve full matrix-valued interaction coefficients with no positivity or definiteness guarantees. This structural difference makes Mamba dynamics substantially harder to analyze and prevents the direct application of existing techniques for attention-based models. To overcome this challenge, we introduce a new analytical framework based on a high-dimensional invariant box and a sharp exit-time argument, which together recover an effective form of sign-definiteness. Using this framework, we characterize the possible limit points of token trajectories and prove explicit exponential convergence rates. Our analysis reveals that the first token has privileged dynamics: its limiting direction attracts subsequent tokens, inducing token clustering and attention-sink phenomena in deep Mamba models. We further show that this attraction mechanism extends to broader sequence dynamics, including state-space models, causal attention, and classical time-series models. Experiments on Falcon-Mamba-7B validate our predictions, showing that concentration on the first token increases with depth and dominates in later layers.

papers.title: Dynamic Optimistic Constrained OCO with Memory via Delay Equivalence
papers.abstract: Online Convex Optimization with memory and time-varying constraints (COCO-M) is a recently-introduced framework that captures the dynamics of stateful online learning and non-stochastic control with budget constraints. Despite its expressive power, COCO-M remains largely understudied. In this work, we tackle this problem in its full scale, providing an optimistic algorithm that incorporates untrusted predictions to tame universal dynamic regret and cumulative constraint violation. Our analysis leverages a potent reduction from memory to delay and treats state-dependent gradients as delayed feedback. We establish the first bounds that adapt to both environment non-stationarity (path length $P_T$) and prediction accuracy, while lifting previous restrictive assumptions such as functional separability. En route to these results, we derive findings of independent interest for the memory-to-delay reduction, and for delayed OCO with time-varying constraints. The proposed framework ensures sublinear worst-case guarantees that improve with prediction accuracy, reaching $\mathcal O(1)$ regret under perfect predictions, with cumulative constraint violation (CCV) $\mathcal O(\sqrt{T})$ for unknown $P_T$ and $\mathcal O(\log T)$ for known or online observable $P_T$ , while recovering the optimal COCO rates when memory disappears.

papers.title: REACT: Towards Real-Time Completion of Skeletal Motion Signals
papers.abstract: Tracking user motion in interactive and immersive applications is increasingly common (e.g., video games, XR systems, smartphones). Yet, processing and transmitting human motion data remain critical challenges, as current approaches strongly rely on the quality of the tracked motion signals. In general, affordable motion-capture systems may produce unnatural animations in the presence of calibration errors, occlusions, sensor drift, high-frequency noise, or other artifacts. More specifically, we simulate occlusions and high-frequency noise and propose to mitigate their effects with REACT, an interactive online motion-completion framework operating causally, frame by frame, without look-ahead. REACT is an S4-based autoregressive model that coordinates complementary motion estimates under specific reliability-dependent constraints and exposes several interpretable internal signals. We present a system-level contribution consisting of a structured formulation of interactive motion completion together with a coherent instantiation of this formulation. We evaluate REACT against several causal baselines and architectural variants under varying levels of occlusion severity, and report their respective inference latencies. Our results show that REACT achieves a relevant compromise between reconstruction accuracy, update smoothness, and interactive inference. Finally, we characterize how its fusion behaviour changes under missing input observations.

papers.title: Polarization cross-talk from non-stationary sources of image jitter
papers.abstract: We generalize a previous formulation for the estimation of polarization cross-talk induced by atmospheric seeing to the case of image jitter that must be described as a non-stationary, and generally non-isotropic, random process. We demonstrate how the newly derived formalism converges towards the previous one in the limit of stationary random image jitter. In the case of non-stationary processes, we compare the predictions of the two formalisms, and illustrate the salient differences. For the sake of demonstration, we adopt for our analysis a specific example of power-spectral density derived from a circulant auto-correlation function, which describes a class of stationary random processes periodic over the length of the time series, and which we successively modified by the insertion of off-diagonal power spectral features at different frequencies in order to test the extended modeling framework for the estimation of polarization cross-talk.

papers.title: Should You Split Decode? Disaggregation Across Future Models and Accelerators
papers.abstract: For large language model (LLM) inference, prefill/decode disaggregation (P/D) is deployed in production to isolate phases with different resource demands. Attention/feed-forward network disaggregation (AFD) splits decode again, but adds communication, placement constraints, and another provisioned pool. We ask whether role-specific placement repays this cost as models and accelerator roadmaps change. Infrastructure is committed before future models and hardware can be benchmarked. We present SiliconForge, a calibrated model that varies the serving decomposition and hardware assignment independently. We compare P/D and P/D+AFD across four model directions, four accelerator classes anchored to current and announced parts, and two fabrics. We co-optimize each design using the same rules for pipeline overlap and the same power budget. Our main comparisons show no robust deployment-level AFD advantage in service-level objective (SLO) goodput per kW. Most nominal estimates favor P/D. The largest AFD lead comes from fitting one more prefill replica, not from a more efficient decode pool. AFD has a nominal lead in the KV-heavy (key-value) model direction when the co-located expert pool spans several small scale-up domains. Larger domains or a fast fabric for both designs weaken that lead. We therefore find that prefill provisioning, decode memory bandwidth, links, and pool granularity decide deployments more than the split alone. A fixed hardware assignment can lose its advantage as models, fabrics, hardware assumptions, and objectives change. Re-optimizing mappings and pool sizes on the same hardware cuts early commitment's median normalized goodput loss from 36% to 9%. We recommend adjustable mappings and pool sizes to let boundary and hardware choices follow model demands.

papers.title: Beyond Quantum Messages: Toward Quantum-Native Network Functioning
papers.abstract: The Quantum Internet is commonly envisioned as a network that transports quantum states and distributes entanglement as the key resource underpinning distributed quantum applications. This view is necessary but incomplete if quantum phenomena are confined to what the network carries or manages, while network functionalities remain grounded predominantly in classical abstractions. This Perspective advances a broader thesis: quantum phenomena can also participate directly in the realization of network functionalities. We first establish the architectural baseline by introducing entanglement as a stateful network resource whose operational condition is non-locally distributed across remote nodes, evolves through manipulation or consumption, and degrades over time through decoherence. Its evolving state must therefore remain visible to the functionalities acting on it. We then move beyond resource visibility and use two mechanisms as proof points of a broader quantum-native functional design space: entanglement generation during propagation through coherent spatial-path superposition, and operational connectivity induced by shared entanglement that can depart from the physical graph. These examples show that paths, neighbors, or participating nodes may become operationally relevant in ways determined by quantum coherence and shared entanglement, rather than by physical connectivity alone. We identify Quantum Addressing as a transversal abstraction capable of representing such relations while complementing, rather than replacing, classical addressing and signaling. The resulting perspective broadens the Quantum Internet from transporting quantum information and distributing entanglement to exploiting quantum phenomena in network functioning, opening a coupled frontier spanning routing, forwarding, control, and functionality placement.

papers.title: A Proximal Newton Framework with Local Superlinear Convergence for Simple Bilevel Optimization
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study a penalty method for simple bilevel optimization in which the lower-level objective has a convex composite structure. Our approach is based on a vanishing-penalty reformulation, which gives rise to a sequence of penalized problems as the penalty parameter decreases. A key difficulty is that metric subregularity of the lower-level optimality mapping does not, in general, yield a uniform error bound for the penalized problems as the penalty parameter vanishes, preventing a direct application of standard proximal Newton theory. To address this difficulty, we first analyze a regularized proximal Newton step by exploiting the specific structure of simple bilevel problems, and establish the local estimates that underpin superlinear convergence. Building on this local analysis, we propose SiB-Newton, which incorporates the proximal Newton step into a globalization strategy. We establish convergence guarantees for SiB-Newton and show that, under suitable local conditions, Newton steps are eventually accepted and the iterates converge at a superlinear rate. Numerical experiments on synthetic examples verify the predicted local superlinear convergence rate.

papers.title: Active model B+ from run-and-tumble particles on a triangular lattice
papers.abstract: Active model B+ (AMB+) explains how motility-induced phase separation can be arrested by reverse Ostwald ripening, but its coefficients have not been derived from a microscopic lattice model that shows it. We provide an exact hydrodynamic description of a six-polarity lattice gas on a hexagonal geometry and employ a full gradient expansion with angular-harmonic elimination to rigorously derive AMB+ with every coefficient fixed by the Péclet number Pe. Near the critical point (3/4, 4), coarsening is ordinary; further away, field theory predicts reverse Ostwald ripening of vapor bubbles above Pe $> 4 \sqrt{3}$, and simulations show long-lived bubbly states.

papers.title: Transformer-Based Trajectory Prescription for sEMG-Optimizing Robot-Mediated Rehabilitation
papers.abstract: Robot-mediated rehabilitation has the potential to deliver high-intensity, individualized therapy, but existing systems (which have not consistently improved outcomes) typically prescribe kinematic trajectories rather than explicitly targeting the neuromotor activations thought to support recovery. To address this gap, and ultimately enable activation-optimizing rehabilitation robot behavior, we present a personalizable transformer-based model mapping individuals' muscle activations (as measured via surface electromyography) to prescribed contact force trajectories when interacting with an end-effector rehabilitation robot. The model uses a transformer encoder-decoder leveraging rotary positional embeddings (RoPE) to generate a latent representation of trajectory-relevant and user-specific neuromotor factors, and augments trajectory prediction with flow matching to produce a distribution over plausible prescriptions biased toward the training distribution. Using data from 16 healthy participants completing 15 isometric trajectory tracking tasks, we evaluate generalization across held-out tasks and users, as well as the feasibility of user-specific fine-tuning within a therapy-session timescale. The model achieves mean trajectory prediction errors of <8% on held out tasks and users, with effectively instantaneous deterministic inference and sub-second sampling of trajectory distributions. An initial test using the model during live rehabilitation tasks demonstrates that, on average, participants reach the target neuromotor activations with just 15% error accumulated throughout the task. These results provide a proof of concept for data-driven, activation-targeted trajectory prescription in robot-mediated rehabilitation and establish a foundation for future validation in clinical populations. Data and code have been open-sourced as part of the OpenRobotRehab project on SimTK.

papers.title: ManimCode: Learning Visual Self-Correction for Educational Animation
papers.abstract: Manim supports precise, programmatic video generation, but a successfully rendered educational animation can still have visual defects, missing explanations, or incorrect content. Rendering does not directly identify the code changes needed to correct these visual failures, so feedback-driven revision is needed. Existing agentic frameworks use iterative rendering and revision but typically rely on large models, often proprietary. Existing Manim datasets primarily contain final programs and often lack quality verification and the trajectories of feedback and revisions needed to learn this refinement process. We introduce ManimData and ManimCode, a data and training framework for feedback-driven educational animation generation. We construct ManimData through a render-guided pipeline that iteratively generates, executes, reviews, and revises Manim programs with retrieved API documentation. Its 24,034 render-verified, quality-filtered records preserve intermediate programs, execution errors, visual critiques, and corrective revisions. We use role-conditioned supervised fine-tuning on these trajectories to train ManimCode, a single 4B model, to write, review, and revise animation programs. To improve correction of errors that differ from those in the collected trajectories, we then train the Reviser with reinforcement learning on self-generated states, using rendering outcomes and reference-free quality feedback. ManimCode achieves 96.6% and 97.0% render success on ManimData-test and ManimBench, compared with 52.6% and 82.0% for the untrained 4B model under the same inference setup, while also improving video quality scores from 2.48 to 2.94 and from 3.00 to 3.44. Integrating ManimCode into two long-form educational video generation systems increases completed videos from 19/117 to 107/117 and from 53/239 to 239/239, alongside improvements in educational effectiveness and visual quality.

papers.title: Dualities in one-dimensional quantum lattice models: Lie groups, Schur-Weyl duality and symmetry breaking
papers.abstract: We present a systematic framework for gauging continuous symmetries, and show that the Schur-Weyl duality arises naturally as a realization of this construction with open boundary conditions. Restricting to compact Lie group symmetries, we construct dual models for one-dimensional quantum lattice models exhibiting those symmetries. We demonstrate that matrix product operators enable the explicit construction of intertwiners between the dual theories and their (non-invertible) symmetries. With closed boundary conditions, we can relate the full spectrum of these dual theories by considering all possible twisted boundary conditions.We illustrate how the Peter-Weyl transform appears when the duality acts on the boundary Hilbert space of a $G$-symmetric model. The presented framework generalizes previous work on dualities for unitary fusion category symmetric models. It exemplifies how dualities for both finite and continuous symmetries rely on the relation between a bond algebra and a representation of the symmetry in the lattice as double centralizers. We argue that dual non-invertible spontaneous symmetry breaking is the mechanism that underlies symmetric tensor network algorithms. We illustrate these results for $U(1)$- and $SU(2)$-symmetric quantum lattice models.

papers.title: Overcompressive shocks in a $2\times2$ hyperbolic system of conservation laws
papers.abstract: Overcompressive shocks in a $2\times2$ hyperbolic system of conservation laws describing small-amplitude longitudinal-torsional waves in an elastic rod are investigated. A viscous regularization method with an anisotropic dissipative matrix is applied to the system. A qualitative analysis of phase portraits has revealed that a two-parameter family of heteroclinic trajectories, representing the structure of an overcompressive shock, exists in one of six domains in the parameter plane. It is established that the model admits overcompressive shocks, which belong to the first type according to the classification of Liu.

papers.title: Gradient higher integrability for a general class of degenerate parabolic double phase systems
papers.abstract: We establish quantitative local higher integrability estimates for weak solutions of degenerate parabolic systems with generalized double phase growth, whose prototype is $$u_t-\operatorname{div}\left(\frac{G'(|Du|)}{|Du|}Du+a(x,t)\frac{H'(|Du|)}{|Du|}Du\right)=0\qquad\text{in }Ω_T.$$ Here $G$ and $H$ are Young functions satisfying suitable structural assumptions. The nonnegative coefficient $a$ is allowed to vanish and has a concave modulus of continuity $ω$ with respect to the parabolic distance. For $Ψ(z,\varkappa)=G(\varkappa)+a(z)H(\varkappa)$, we prove that solutions in $L^\infty(0,T;L^s(Ω,\mathbb{R}^N))$, $2\le s<\infty$, satisfy $Ψ(\cdot,|Du|)\in L^{1+\varepsilon}_{\mathrm{loc}}$ for some $\varepsilon>0$, provided $$\limsup_{ρ\to 0+}ω(ρ)\frac{H(ρ^{-\frac{n+s}{s}})}{G(ρ^{-\frac{n+s}{s}})}<\infty.$$ For bounded solutions, the corresponding condition involves $H(ρ^{-1})/G(ρ^{-1})$. These conditions extend the known interpolative gap bounds from power growth to general growth functions and continuity moduli. In particular, for $G(\varkappa)=\varkappa^p$, $H(\varkappa)=\varkappa^q$, and $ω(ρ)\simeqρ^α$, they recover $q\le p+sα/(n+s)$ and $q\le p+α$, respectively. The proof combines an intrinsic stopping-time argument with inverse-function estimates to derive Poincaré and reverse Hölder inequalities adapted to the general growth phases.

papers.title: AutoCompress: Automated Hardware-Guided Model Compression
papers.abstract: LLM pruning must preserve quality while meeting hardware- and workload-specific constraints on latency, throughput, and memory. Existing pruning workflows often target parameter counts, requiring practitioners to manually select model sizes that meet latency, throughput, and GPU memory limits. However, parameter count alone does not predict these metrics, which depend on the model architecture, workload, hardware, and serving engine. We introduce AutoCompress, a hardware-guided compression framework that directly incorporates such constraints into differentiable architecture search. AutoCompress jointly optimizes global and per-layer structure to produce heterogeneous architectures, guided by serving-engine cost models validated against end-to-end latency, throughput, and memory measurements. We evaluate AutoCompress on long-context local coding, batched datacenter serving, and latency-sensitive in-game interaction. Compared to the state-of-the-art Minitron pruning framework, AutoCompress improves average accuracy across eight benchmarks by 6.57, 2.35, and 0.57 percentage points on RTX 5070, RTX 5080, and H100, respectively. AutoCompress also compresses Nemotron 3.5 Super from 120B to 74B parameters for single-B200 BF16 serving at 128K context, retaining 95% of its mean benchmark score.

papers.title: Fourier level inequalities on the discrete cube via complex hypercontractivity and Riesz transforms
papers.abstract: Eldan's level-$1{:}3$ inequality is a central tool in his second-order correlation inequalities for increasing Boolean functions. His proof is going to Gaussian space and uses an entropy estimate for second Hermite tensors. We give a direct proof on the discrete hypercube. For increasing real-valued functions $f,g:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, we prove $$ W_3[f,g]\ge -2W_1[f,g]\log\!\left(\frac{\sqrt{\mathrm{Var}(f)\mathrm{Var}(g)}}{W_1[f,g]}\right). $$ The proof combines complex hypercontractivity with the discrete Riesz transforms. We also give a short proof of a level-$1:d$ inequality obtained by Keller and Kindler. As an application, we recover Eldan's correlation inequality with a slight improvement. If $f,g:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}$ are increasing and $g$ is antipodal, then $$ \mathrm{Cov}(f,g)\ge \frac1{24}\,\frac{\sum_i\mathrm{Inf}_i[f]\mathrm{Inf}_i[g]}{\sqrt{\log\!\left(4e\sqrt{\mathrm{Var}(f)\mathrm{Var}(g)}/(\sum_i\mathrm{Inf}_i[f]\mathrm{Inf}_i[g])\right)}}, $$ where the square-root logarithm cannot be improved as shown in the OR--majority example.

papers.title: Hierarchical Incremental Beta Splatting for Online Reconstruction
papers.abstract: Online 3D Gaussian Splatting reconstructs a scene during capture: each keyframe spawns primitives once and refines them for only a few dozen iterations, leaving little chance to fix poor initialization or missing detail. Gaussians are also inherently soft, needing many overlaps for solid surfaces. We present Hierarchical Incremental Beta Splatting (HIBS), which brings beta kernels to incremental reconstruction. Their shape parameter interpolates between a soft, Gaussian-like profile and a flat-topped, near-opaque surfel, acting as a confidence dial for geometry. Our confidence-aware spawning uses geometric observability and multi-view depth agreement to initialize both opacity and shape, producing solid primitives where geometry is verifiable and soft, correctable primitives where it is not. As online densification, error-driven relocation recycles stale primitives into photometric-error hotspots. Bounded beta kernel support enables exact tile culling and faster rasterization, and a closed-form, shape-preserving merging formulation provides a level-of-detail (LOD) hierarchy for fast optimization and real-time rendering. On Mip-NeRF 360 in the on-the-fly protocol, HIBS improves PSNR by up to 0.8 dB while reducing optimization time by up to 40%. Project page: https://linus-franke.com/hibs/

papers.title: Machine learning classification of dynamical phases in a driven nonlinear Su-Schrieffer-Heeger lattice
papers.abstract: Driven nonlinear photonic lattices can settle into steady, symmetry-broken, periodic, or chaotic states, and mapping where each occurs in parameter space is key to device design. Brute-force mapping is slow and relies on hand-built criteria, while machine-learning classifiers are usually tested on different systems, so it is unclear which suits a new lattice. We therefore apply four classifiers to the same coherently driven Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) chain of Kerr resonators: a hand-built heuristic classifier based on Lyapunov exponents and spectral diagnostics, a supervised convolutional neural network (CNN) trained on the heuristic labels, an unsupervised library-building scheme based on augmented dynamic mode decomposition (aDMD), and an unsupervised Gaussian mixture model (GMM) on four dynamical invariants that include an aDMD reconstruction error. Using a converged heuristic diagram as the reference, the CNN reaches 98.0% held-out accuracy, while the two label-free methods reach adjusted Rand indices (ARIs) of 0.916 and 0.947, respectively, without seeing any labels. We show that the aDMD library cleanly resolves the stable and bistable phases and separates symmetric from symmetry-broken periodic oscillations, which the heuristic misses, though it cannot distinguish periodic from chaotic switching. We also find that a poorly converged reference understates the label-free methods' accuracy.

papers.title: Interactive Visual Gym: Evaluating Visual Interaction Models with Simulated Users in Interactive Worlds
papers.abstract: Visual interaction models that support users during ongoing physical tasks require evaluation in closed loop, where assistant responses can change subsequent user behavior and task outcomes. Existing benchmarks largely rely on offline replay and therefore cannot capture these effects. We introduce Interactive Visual Gym, a framework for closed-loop evaluation and training of visual interaction models through joint simulation of executable task environments and human users. We contribute three simulators that recreate everyday tasks and human-aligned action spaces across cooking, household manipulation, and mobile-interface domains, together with a persona-conditioned user simulation harness that collaborates with the assistant while incorporating controlled execution errors and other out-of-plan behaviors. We instantiate the framework as IVG-Bench, a benchmark with 315 interaction scenarios. Evaluating state-of-the-art VLMs as visual interaction models reveals substantial limitations: the best-performing model, Gemini 4 Argon, completes only 53.4% of tasks within the time limit, exhibits significant weaknesses in factual grounding and actionable guidance, and is often too slow to prevent errors when response latency is considered. We verify our evaluation protocol with a human study which finds 78.5% agreement between our interaction-quality metric and participant preferences. We further show that the environments provide useful learning signals: in a proof-of-concept GRPO experiment, closed-loop training improves both task success and interaction quality for Qwen3.5-4B model in our cooking environment.

papers.title: Hard Issue, Weak Model, or Bad Run? Rethinking Failure Prediction for Coding Agents
papers.abstract: Trajectory-based failure predictors for software engineering (SE) agents read the partial trajectory of a run to flag whether it is going right or wrong. If it is going wrong, the run can be stopped, retried, or switched to another model. We ask whether these predictors learn anything about the run itself. On public SWE-bench Verified trajectories, where each model attempts each issue once, two run-independent factors dominate predictor performance. The first is issue difficulty: a reference score that never looks at the run, only at how hard the issue is for other models, reaches 0.92 AUROC, whereas trajectory predictors reach about 0.62. The second is model ability: within an issue, knowing which model ran predicts failure better than our predictors do, and the predictors largely reproduce the overall ability ranking of the models. Beyond difficulty and ability, what predictors gain from the trajectory is statistically equivalent to zero. This confusion carries over to the actions taken after a prediction. Model switching is often motivated by the gap between the best single model's resolution rate and an any-model oracle. This gap is no larger than random variation alone produces. Per-issue switching gains nothing on held-out runs. In a repeated-run pilot, the same model often solves an issue in some runs and fails it in others. Retrying thus has real room to repair failures, but it rescues only failures caused by a bad run, not those on an issue beyond the model's ability. Current predictors cannot tell the causes apart, as they mostly predict the issue and the model, not the run. We call for failure prediction that explains why a run fails, evaluated on repeated-run benchmarks and in closed-loop, equal-budget settings.

papers.title: A Generative Model of Contextual Integrity: Appropriate vs. Inappropriate Information Sharing
papers.abstract: Contextual integrity (CI) holds that appropriate information flow depends on context-specific norms. The same disclosure may be appropriate in one context and inappropriate in another. We build a generative model of contextual integrity to study information sharing through simulated conversations. Two actors played by large language models exchange messages, with one holding private information and the other seeking it. We examine how sharing and refusal vary with the situation, the holder's decision logic, disposition, and the underlying language model. Actors shared information with the rightful recipients when it was needed, but also disclosed it to people who were not entitled to receive it. The model provides a way to study how disclosure and refusal develop through conversation as the situations and the actors vary.

papers.title: A centroaffine perspective on improved Brascamp--Lieb and dimensional Brunn--Minkowski inequalities
papers.abstract: We study dimensional concavity properties of even log-concave measures within the framework of weighted centroaffine differential geometry. We express the relevant local concavity inequalities in terms of a weighted Hilbert--Brunn--Minkowski operator and establish an anisotropic Poincaré inequality for odd functions and a strengthened Brascamp--Lieb inequality for even functions. As applications, we obtain quantitative dimensional concavity estimates for a class of geometric measures and measures with pinched Hessian, extending results of Cordero-Erausquin and Rotem for rotationally invariant measures and Eskenazis and Moschidis for the Gaussian measure.

papers.title: Mitigating scanning-induced systematics in Hipparcos and implications for Gaia astrometry
papers.abstract: Space-based astrometric missions such as Hipparcos and Gaia rely on one-dimensional scanning strategies that couple the measured signals with both observation times and scanning geometry. This coupling can introduce spurious periodicities and complicate their interpretation. We present a non-parametric extension of the phase-distance correlation (PDC) periodogram that quantifies and reduces dependence on scan geometry at the period-search stage. Using Hipparcos data, we identified recurrent periodicities associated with characteristic scanning-law timescales and showed that they are strongly suppressed by the scan-angle-controlled statistic. We then applied the method to Gaia Data Release 4 (DR4) prerelease epoch astrometry, where a recurrent ~54-day feature is suppressed across multiple sources while independently known orbital signals remain detectable. The method provides a diagnostic of scan-angle dependence and a way to mitigate its impact on period searches. These results are particularly relevant for Gaia DR4, where public epoch astrometry will enable large-scale searches for companions ranging from exoplanets to dormant black holes.

papers.title: Multimodal-SEA: Benchmarking AI Agent Security under Multimodal Social Engineering Attacks
papers.abstract: Personal AI agents face social engineering attacks supported by forged multimodal content, but existing evaluations mainly focus on text-based dialogue, leaving their intrinsic security under such attacks insufficiently studied. We introduce Multimodal-SEA, an interactive benchmark comprising 608 expert-designed tasks grounded in real-world fraud cases, covering 14 domains and 152 attack scenarios with prepared multimodal content. The tasks span four difficulty levels and reflect the distinct social and cultural contexts of Chinese and English environments. Agents inspect content, verify requests, and execute actions in simulated applications, with attack outcomes grounded in verifiable tool execution logs. To enable controlled red teaming of personal agents, we design a multimodal attack harness that integrates task information, attack progression control, and multimodal content construction to evaluate their intrinsic security against adaptive social engineering attacks in simulated environments. Evaluating seven widely used multimodal models across six dimensions reveals that all are vulnerable, with attack success rates of 7.1% to 34.5%. Adding multimodal content increases attack success from 19.9% to 29.2%, despite increased proactive verification coverage. Stronger safety instructions reduce attack success without improving recognition of deceptive multimodal content, while lower attack success rates for some models accompany excessive refusal of legitimate requests.

papers.title: Dynamical Keldysh model for colored noise and finite relaxation rate
papers.abstract: The Keldysh model describes quantum dots subjected to Gaussian noise with infinite correlation time. For multi-component noise coupled through non-commuting matrices, the spectrum exhibits a pseudogap. We solve the model for coloured noise with any correlation time, $1/ γ$. Finite memory leads to the pseudogap being filled, its peaks merging and the line narrowing.

papers.title: Has Quarkyonic Matter Been Seen in Lattice Simulations?
papers.abstract: Quarkyonic Matter refers to the dual state of matter between confined hadrons and quasi-free quarks. This duality leads to a robust constraint on the behavior of the distribution functions. After a comprehensive review of Quarkyonic Matter based on the distribution functions, we discuss recent lattice data for two-color QCD in $(1+1)$ and $(3+1)$ dimensions at finite baryon number density and QCD in $(3+1)$ dimensions at finite isospin density, as well as the astrophysically inferred equation of state. Taken together, these results reveal a coherent picture consistent with the emergence of Quarkyonic Matter in lattice simulations. Future lattice calculations of baryon and gauge-invariant quark momentum distributions at high density would provide a more direct test of this interpretation.

papers.title: Construction and performance evaluation of a meter-scale monolithic scintillator tracker with embedded scatterers
papers.abstract: A meter-scale Fiber-Readout mOnolithic and Scatterer-embedded scintillator Tracker (FROST) was constructed and operated in the NINJA experiment to enable muon-track matching between the nuclear emulsion detectors and the downstream muon detector. The detector consists of a 1.32 m $\times$ 1.40 m plastic scintillator plate assembled from optically bonded scatterer-embedded plates, with wavelength-shifting fibers arranged at a pitch of 10 mm. During J-PARC neutrino-beam operation, FROST achieved a data acquisition efficiency of 99.59% and a detection efficiency of 99.946$\pm$0.006% for selected neutrino-induced muons well within the active area. A position reconstruction method based on the light-yield distribution was developed for both single- and multi-particle events. In a neutrino-interaction simulation, muon position resolutions of 1.77 mm and 1.61 mm were achieved in the two orthogonal readout directions, assuming correct muon identification. Using a beam-data sample dominated by single-muon events, upper limits on the position resolution of 2.20 mm and 2.03 mm were obtained for track angles below 20°. These results demonstrate that the FROST concept can be scaled up to a meter-scale active area while maintaining high detection efficiency and a position resolution well below the readout pitch under actual experimental conditions.
